conviction_note: abs_move 5.0 (between the name's own 3.24% median and its 5.14% max; the 8.03% option-implied move comes off a 36%-wide ATM spread and is indicative only) times a 53 p_up. The two measurements roughly agree: impact_sum is +0.4. The mid-quarter update points to a clean Q3 (lower ECR cost, NPLs down about 10%, NCOs below Q2). The Q4 mortgage and warehouse outlook has turned against the July guide since mortgage rates hit 7.40%. The stock already fell from $79 to $74 on that, sell-side targets were cut into the print and puts are bid. Net, a thin lean up and nothing decisive.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS $2.43 on revenue of $988.95m (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/WAL, fetched 2026-10-19). Benzinga has $2.46 on $992.5m (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WAL/price-targets, via search snippet, 403 on fetch). The two sources agree within $0.03, so the bar is usable. The company gave no EPS guide. Its 2026 outlook (Q2 deck, slide 17: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001212545/000162828026049001/walq22026earningspresent.htm) is NII +12-14%, non-interest income +13-17%, ECR deposit costs $650-700m, NCOs 25-35bp, loans +$5bn, deposits +$6bn, and mortgage banking 'in line to Q2 for the next two quarters', assuming a 25bp September hike. Q2 actual was EPS $2.36 and revenue $995.7m.
positioning_check: Short interest is 6,219,780 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, about 5.7% of shares outstanding, 4.73 days to cover, up from about 2.3m in late April and near the 6.30m peak of 2026-07-31 (Equibles from FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/wal/shortinterest, fetched 2026-10-19). That is elevated and rising, but not a crowded short. The 25-delta skew is +5.73 vol points (downside paid) and put/call OI is 2.02 on only 2,216 contracts. The stock is -5.47% over 20d, -22.6% from its 52-week high and +11.5% off its low. A Form 4 cash-RSU settlement priced the stock at $79.03 on 2026-09-15 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1212545/000162828026062566/wk-form4_1789678894.xml), so it is down about 6% since the Barclays mid-quarter update. The sell side cut targets into the print (stockanalysis.com headlines with relative dates): Wells $90->84, TD Cowen $90->85, JPM $93->90, Citi $98->95, RBC $95->93 and Truist $93->84, against a Barclays raise from $88->93.

findings.finding: At Barclays on 2026-09-16 the CEO gave a mid-quarter Q3 update. $2.5bn of high-cost deposits had already moved off balance sheet in Q3, against the roughly $750m still guided in July. ECR expense will be down about $10m QoQ in Q3 (Q2 total deposit costs were $179.2m). Adjusted NIM is up 'several bp' and headline NIM down about 1bp. NPLs are expected to fall about 10%, from $567m to about $500m, with four of six large problem credits resolved. NCOs will be below Q2's $55m (37bp) in both rate and dollars, and ACL/NPL coverage 'well over 100%'. Q3 buybacks will be slightly more than half of the $150m H2 plan. Against a consensus of $2.43 (Q2 was $2.36), a lower provision (Q2 was $80.4m) plus about $10m less ECR is worth roughly $0.10-0.20 of EPS before any fee or NII drag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit is the line WAL trades on. The fraud-loan disclosure of Oct 2025 cost -10.8% in a day (Glancy Law page). Of the last 7 prints, 5 rose (median |move| 3.24%), including +3.24% on 2025-10-21 and +3.61% on 2026-07-21, a print that slightly missed consensus. The Q1 2026 LAM charge-off print moved only +0.69%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The update was public a month ago and the stock has fallen about 6% since, on rates and mortgage. If the cleaner-credit Q3 were fully reflected, the downside skew and the target cuts would have eased. Both widened. The part not priced is the size of the provision release relative to an EPS bar only $0.07 above Q2.
findings.independence: Q2 call, July: management guided the nonaccrual trend 'down between now and year end' and H2 NCOs 'a little above the midpoint of 25-35bp' (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-western-alliance-bancorporation-stock/). Same management, so not independent. Peer credit is in the separate finding below.

findings.finding: The Freddie Mac 30-year rate went from about 6.55% in mid-July to 7.03% on 2026-09-24 and 7.40% on 2026-10-08/15, the highest in more than a year. The July guide held mortgage banking 'in line to Q2 for the next two quarters' (Q2 was $53.4m gain on sale plus $31.3m net servicing) and expected only a seasonal Q4 warehouse decline. That was set when rates were about 6.5-6.7%. A cut to the Q4 mortgage-banking and non-interest-income outlook is the likely guidance revision, partly offset by MSR value gains and lower 90%-beta warehouse ECR cost as balances fall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026 print: non-interest income guide cut from +20-25% to +13-17% and loans and deposits trimmed, yet the stock rose +3.61% on the print. Earnings Whispers records a -5.1% post-earnings drift after it. So a fee-guide cut alone was not sold on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The stock fell from $79 on 9/15 to $74 as rates rose, and the target cuts cluster in late Sep and early Oct. The unpriced part is the size of the Q4 mortgage cut and whether management also trims NII or the loan guide. A fully priced case would show the skew normalising into the print, and it has not.
findings.independence: Q2 deck slide 17 has the 'in line to Q2' mortgage guide and the September-hike assumption (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001212545/000162828026049001/walq22026earningspresent.htm). The ClearValue Lending piece of 2026-09-04 shows rates from 6.55% to 6.71% and refinance applications -6% in that week (https://clearvaluelending.com/blog/mortgage-rates-13-month-high-september-2026). This is a macro proxy: the company has not confirmed any change.

findings.finding: Peer read-through on mortgage warehouse: First Horizon's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-15) shows loans to mortgage companies of $3,869m at period end, down $891m (-19%) QoQ from $4,759m. That points to lower period-end warehouse loans at WAL, one of the largest warehouse lenders, and to lower associated ECR deposits. It is a headwind to reported loan growth against the +$5bn 2026 guide and to period-end deposits, and partly offsets itself through lower ECR expense.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No documented WAL reaction to a warehouse-balance surprise in the baseline. Q2 2026 period-end deposits fell 1.0% QoQ and the stock rose +3.61%.
findings.why_not_priced: The peer print came after WAL last spoke on 9/16 and is a line item in another bank's release, not a WAL headline. If it were priced, WAL loan estimates would have been cut along with the targets, and that cannot be verified. Its value is limited because WAL is deliberately capping loan growth to fund buybacks, so a lower warehouse balance is close to a choice the market has already accepted.
findings.independence: Shares the rate driver with the mortgage-rate finding above but lands on a different line, the reported Q3 balance sheet rather than the Q4 guide. The FHN number is a different document. It is a proxy: WAL has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16. That is exactly the hike WAL's revised July outlook assumed. Management describes the bank as asset-sensitive on NII and rate-neutral on earnings at risk, with ECR betas of about 90% on warehouse and about 50% on its other ECR businesses. The hike lands inside the guide, so it is expected to leave the NII and deposit-cost ranges unchanged.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No WAL print has turned on a rate decision that it pre-assumed.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced because it is inside the guide. It is filed so the panel can see that the rate path matched the company's assumption and is not a surprise in either direction.
findings.independence: Q2 call quote: 'Our new outlook incorporates a 25-basis-point hike in September' (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-western-alliance-bancorporation-stock/).

findings.finding: Positioning was de-risked into the print. Short interest rose from about 2.3m shares (late April) to 6.22m (2026-09-30, 5.7% of shares outstanding, 4.73 days to cover). At least five brokers cut targets from late September into October (Wells $84, TD Cowen $85, Truist $84, JPM $90, Citi $95). The 25-delta skew is +5.7 vol points to the downside and the stock is down about 6% since the 9/16 update. That lowers the effective bar for a print management already pre-signalled as clean on credit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: rose +3.61% on a slight EPS miss, with the stock already down into the print. Oct 2025: +3.24% after the fraud-driven selloff the week before.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew and the target cuts are the market's own statement, so this item sits against the price, not inside it. If the bearish positioning were wrong and already corrected, the skew would be near zero and short interest falling, and neither holds. Short interest is 5.7%, not crowded, so this is a modest tilt and not a squeeze setup.
findings.independence: Target cuts are listed on stockanalysis.com with relative dates (https://www.stockanalysis.com/stocks/wal/, fetched 2026-10-19). The skew is in the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: Peer credit was benign in Q3 2026. Regions (10/16) reported NCOs down 13bp to 29bp, lower NPLs and an EPS beat ($0.73 adjusted vs $0.66). First Horizon (10/15) reported NPLs down $49m to $482m and NCOs of 22bp. Truist (10/16) reported adjusted EPS of $1.16, up 12% YoY. No new fund-finance or NDFI fraud shock has surfaced among peers that reported before WAL.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: WAL's large moves have come from idiosyncratic credit, not peer read-throughs. In Oct 2025 it fell with Zions on its own fraud disclosure.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, since peer prints are public. Analysts cut targets on Regions and PNC on 10/19 (MarketBeat) despite the beats, so clean credit is not being rewarded sector-wide. Hence the small size.
findings.independence: First Horizon Q3 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036966/000003696626000178/a3q2026earningsrelease.htm) and Truist Q3 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000092230/000009223026000108/ex991-3q26.htm). This is a sector proxy, not WAL's own number. Zions reports the same evening, so it cannot be read in advance.

outside_window.finding: Litigation with Jefferies/Point Bonita over the $126.4m First Brands-related loan that WAL charged off in Q1 2026: WAL sued in March 2026, Jefferies counter-sued in July 2026 over a frozen $25m account. Any recovery would be a gain, but no ruling or settlement is dated inside the window.
Basel III re-proposal (March 2026): management cites about 80bp of CET1 benefit if rules are finalised, which would allow larger buybacks. No final rule had been published as of 2026-10-19.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR submissions since 2026-07-21: only the dividend 8-K (7/30), the 10-Q (7/31), 13G filings and routine monthly cash-RSU Form 4 settlements (e.g. CFO, 123 units at $79.03 on 9/15). No new 8-K, credit disclosure or insider open-market selling.
Q3 2026 sell-side previews with reasoning behind the October target cuts: only headlines found, no notes.
October 2026 MBA weekly application data: not found. Only July 2026 releases and the Freddie Mac/FRED rate series.
New WAL borrower-fraud or NDFI court filings after July 2026: none found beyond the Jefferies/Point Bonita cases.
KRE/KBW regional index performance in October 2026: no dated coverage found.

baseline_tension: The findings net slightly positive (clean credit pre-signalled, positioning de-risked) against a +5.7 vol-point put skew and a -5.5% 20-day run-up. The negatives I found (mortgage rates at 7.4%, lower warehouse balances) agree with the skew and are probably what it prices, so the positive lean is kept small and p_up held at 53.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): the Barclays credit/ECR finding lands inside what management pre-signalled on 9/16, so it was cut from +0.8 to +0.5.
Rule 5 (macro proxy): the mortgage-rate Q4-guide finding has no company confirmation, so it was cut from -0.7 to -0.5. It also agrees with the skew (rule 7), so it is likely priced.
Rules 5 and 9 (net of the rest): the FHN warehouse read-through was cut from -0.3 to -0.2 because lower warehouse balances also cut the 90%-beta ECR expense and loan growth is capped by choice.

Rule 7: short interest was checked before filing the negatives. It is 5.7% and not crowded, so it did not shrink them further. The positioning finding was cut from +0.5 to +0.4 because it argues against a strong skew.
Rule 5: the peer-credit proxy was cut from +0.3 to +0.2.
The Fed-hike finding (0.0), abs_move_pct and p_up were left unchanged.
